title: Qes Beqes (Slowly, Slowly)
logline: A girl learning to bake injera wants to quit after her first torn attempts, until her mother puts an egg in her palm and reminds her how slowly good things grow.
feel: Relief and permission to go slowly: small steady steps count as progress.
style_block: flat illustrated storybook style, warm earth tones of ochre, terracotta and cream, soft paper texture, gentle morning light, no text, no letters
character: THE GIRL: a 12-year-old Ethiopian girl with black braided hair, large expressive brown eyes, a mustard-yellow dress and a white cotton shawl. HER MOTHER: a woman in her late thirties with a white cotton netela shawl with a green-and-red border and a headscarf, kind face, often shown only as hands or from behind. SETTING: a small warm family kitchen with a clay mitad griddle, a woven basket of eggs, and sunlight through one window.

shots.reason: Establish the one place and plant the egg motif in the first image.
shots.keyframe_prompt: wide view of a small warm family kitchen at dawn, clay griddle on a low stove, a woven basket of eggs in the foreground, sunlight through the window
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.narration: በአንዲት ትንሽ ኩሽና ውስጥ፣ አንዲት ልጅ እንጀራ መጋገር እየተማረች ነበር።
shots.subtitle: In a small kitchen, a girl was learning to bake injera.

shots.reason: Introduce the girl and the first failure: a torn injera on the griddle.
shots.keyframe_prompt: the girl standing over a clay griddle looking at a torn, uneven injera, flour on her hands, medium shot
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.subtitle: Her first injera tore. So did the second.

shots.reason: Show the low point: discouragement, the moment the audience recognises themselves.
shots.keyframe_prompt: the girl sitting on a low stool with her head down, a burnt injera on a plate beside her, close-up, soft shadows
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.narration: ሦስተኛው ተቃጠለ። ልጅቷ ሁሉንም ለመተው ፈለገች።
shots.subtitle: The third one burned. The girl wanted to quit.

shots.reason: Introduce the mother quietly, as hands only, and the egg that carries the proverb.
shots.keyframe_prompt: close-up of a mother's hands lifting one egg from a woven basket, warm light, only hands and sleeve visible
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.narration: እናቷ ምንም ሳትናገር ከቅርጫቱ ውስጥ አንድ እንቁላል አነሳች።
shots.subtitle: Her mother said nothing. She took an egg from the basket.

shots.reason: The turn: the mother speaks the proverb. First of at most two full views of her.
shots.keyframe_prompt: the mother kneeling to the girl's height and placing an egg gently into the girl's open palm, both faces warm and calm, medium shot
shots.speaker: mother
shots.subtitle: Slowly, slowly, an egg walks on its own legs.

shots.reason: Compress weeks of practice into one image so the audience feels time pass.
shots.keyframe_prompt: the girl pouring batter onto the griddle, a stack of imperfect injera beside her, sun moving across the kitchen wall, hopeful expression
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.narration: ቀናት አለፉ፤ ሳምንታትም አለፉ። በየቀኑ ደግማ ሞከረች።
shots.subtitle: Days passed, then weeks. Every day, she tried again.

shots.reason: The payoff: the first perfect injera, the image the audience should remember.
shots.keyframe_prompt: close-up of a perfectly round, soft injera with fine eyes on the clay griddle, steam rising in golden light, the girl's proud smile blurred behind
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.narration: አንድ ማለዳ፣ እንጀራው ክብ እና ለስላሳ ሆኖ ወጣ።
shots.subtitle: One morning, the injera came out round and soft.

shots.reason: Emotional landing: the egg returns to the basket and mother and daughter share a quiet smile.
shots.keyframe_prompt: the girl placing the egg back into the woven basket as her mother smiles beside her, the finished injera on a plate, warm golden light, wide shot
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.subtitle: Slowly, slowly, the egg had walked.
